assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TNF as the dominant driver in the cytokine network of rheumatoid synovium, followed by proof-of-concept clinical blockade, is a textbook bench-to-bedside discovery. It transformed rheumatoid arthritis, spondyloarthritis, psoriasis and inflammatory bowel disease, and established cytokine-targeted therapy as a drug class. Originality and clarity are high; a clear causal chain runs from mechanism to patient outcome.
assessment.attribution: The Feldmann-Maini pairing is the natural and widely recognized one: Feldmann supplied the mechanistic insight and in vitro work, Maini led the clinical trials. The credited list is exactly two, so there is no truncation problem. Other contributors (e.g. antibody developers, TNF cloning groups) are outside the supplied credit and would be a possible objection.
assessment.maturity: Over 25 years of use with extensive independent confirmation, multiple biologics, and long-term safety data. Recognition is, if anything, overdue. I work in this clinical field, so I would flag that my familiarity should be balanced by colleagues, but I have no documented personal involvement with the candidates.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views the discovery as sufficiently original versus the antibody-engineering and cloning steps by others
Priority and credit allocation among TNF biology pioneers beyond the two credited names is not resolved by the supplied text

assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and the development of long-acting agonists have produced one of the most consequential therapeutic advances in decades, with demonstrated effects on glycemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. The discovery chain is clear: proglucagon processing, incretin action, then durable pharmacology.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is the main difficulty: four credited names and a known priority discussion about the identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide (Mojsov, Habener, Holst) versus Drucker's physiology and Knudsen's drug design. A three-person configuration of Drucker, Holst and Knudsen reflects physiology, peptide biology and translation, but it leaves out Mojsov, which would be contested.
assessment.maturity: Clinical confirmation is large and independent, with outcome trials. Timing is very mature and the field is arguably at its peak recognition moment. Some newer indications and long-term safety are still being established, though that does not undermine the core discovery.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among Mojsov, Holst, Habener (not on list) and Drucker is contested
Whether industry-based drug design (Knudsen) belongs in a scientific discovery prize alongside basic physiology

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new modality, living drugs. Originality, clinical impact and conceptual clarity are strong, and the principle extends to other diseases including early autoimmune applications.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain are the most decisive credited figures, with Sadelain for CAR design including costimulation and June for first successful clinical translation in CLL. Rosenberg's adoptive-cell therapy work is foundational but is partly distinct. Eshhar and others outside the credited names are a potential gap I cannot resolve from the list.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and several years of follow-up, with independent confirmation. Solid-tumour efficacy and toxicity management remain limited, but the core discovery is mature enough. Timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Distinct roles of first-generation CAR concepts versus costimulatory design and clinical translation
Rosenberg's inclusion versus the CAR-specific work is a judgment call
Long-term safety, including secondary malignancies, still maturing

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 was identified at the t(14;18) translocation in follicular lymphoma, and the work revealed that cancer can arise from blocked cell death rather than only increased proliferation. This led to the BH3-mimetic venetoclax and a general framework for apoptosis regulation. Importance and lasting impact are high, and the story is conceptually clean.
assessment.attribution: Adams and Cory defined the Bcl-2 family function in lymphoma and the apoptotic network at Walter and Eliza Hall; Vaux showed BCL-2 as a death inhibitor with genetic evidence. The supplied list of four includes Strasser; a three-person configuration is plausible but the Tsujimoto and Croce contributions to the original translocation cloning are not in the credit and may be contested.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently through decades of work and by an approved targeted therapy in CLL and AML. Mature and timely.
uncertainties: Priority for cloning of BCL2 at the translocation (Tsujimoto, Croce, Cleary) is outside the supplied credit
Whether the prize would be framed around apoptosis regulation or the targeted therapy

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR as a central controller of growth and nutrient response is a foundational discovery in cell and metabolic physiology, with ramifications in cancer, immunology (T-cell fate), ageing and transplantation (rapamycin). Originality and conceptual unity are strong.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genetically and defined its function in yeast, which I regard as the decisive contribution. Sabatini identified mTOR and mTORC1 and nutrient-sensing pathways in mammals. Schreiber's work on FKBP-rapamycin is important chemical biology but arguably less central. Brown and Sabatini's mTOR identification and Heitman, Hall and Movva's yeast work show parallel priority questions.
assessment.maturity: Widely confirmed across systems with clinical use of rapalogs, though clinical efficacy of mTOR inhibitors beyond transplantation and some cancers is more modest than the mechanistic importance. Recognition timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Potential allocation disputes among Hall, Sabatini, Schreiber and the independent mammalian identification groups
Concerns about the standing of one laureate candidate are not addressed in the supplied text

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new form of organelle-to-nucleus signalling that is central to proteostasis and relevant to diabetes, neurodegeneration, cancer and immune cell differentiation. The discovery is original, mechanistically elegant and broadly general.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently delineated the Ire1-Hac1 pathway in yeast and the mammalian ATF6 route; this two-person configuration is natural and fair. Ron and others on mammalian PERK/IRE1 arms are not in the credited names, which leaves some allocation uncertainty.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across species for decades. Clinical translation is still emerging, so the recognition would rest on basic biology rather than therapy, which is acceptable for a mature discovery of this type.
uncertainties: Contributions from the mammalian PERK and IRE1 groups are not part of the supplied credit

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway explains how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity and interferon production, linking infection, autoimmunity (including interferonopathies and lupus-related biology), cancer immunology and ageing. Conceptual impact is high, and the discovery is mechanistically clear.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cyclic dinucleotide second messenger cGAMP, which I regard as the decisive step. Barber identified STING; Ishikawa is also a STING co-discoverer. The unlisted early STING and cyclic dinucleotide literature (e.g. Vance, Sauer) adds complexity. A two-person configuration of Chen and Barber is defensible, though contestable.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature, with extensive independent confirmation and genetic human disease, but therapeutic application is still unproven (STING agonists and antagonists in trials). Recognition is somewhat early relative to other candidates.
uncertainties: Clinical validation of therapeutic targeting is not yet established
Credit between Barber and Ishikawa for STING identification, and the relation to cyclic dinucleotide signalling in bacteria

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification and cloning of IL-6 (B-cell stimulatory factor 2) and development of IL-6 receptor blockade (tocilizumab) established IL-6 as a driver of rheumatoid arthritis, Castleman disease, cytokine release syndrome and other inflammatory conditions. The discovery is clear and clinically important.
assessment.attribution: Kishimoto and Hirano cloned IL-6 and elaborated its receptor system; the two-person credit is coherent. Others also contributed to IL-6 identification (e.g. Sehgal, Content, Poupart), so priority is not unambiguous.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed, with approved therapies for decades. It overlaps conceptually with a TNF-type cytokine-blockade prize, so the committee would need to decide if both belong or if one would be recognized first.
uncertainties: Overlap with TNF blockade as a cytokine-targeting theme
Parallel identification of the same molecule by several groups in the 1980s
